Something I tell every group on day one. The best questions in this room will not come from the panel, and they will not come from the people who speak the most. They come from the people who are quiet for forty minutes and then ask the one thing nobody else noticed. So if you are sitting there thinking your English is not good enough to ask, please hear this: nobody is grading your grammar. They are listening to the question. And a slow question in careful English lands better than a fast one that says nothing. One more thing. Write it down before you raise your hand. Everybody does that. The people who look confident are just the ones who prepared the sentence.

Can I ask how you sold that to your team? Because in my case, honestly, that conversation did not go well. Right, so you split the target by quarter instead of by year. And people accepted that? Interesting. Would you mind if I emailed you about it next week? I would like to try it, and I would rather not repeat your mistakes. That is a joke. Partly.
